title: NudgeStreamer.collectNudge credits the buffer with the amount SENT, not received, against a POOLED per-token balance — one taxed token drains sibling streams and bricks batchMint for every reward token
description: `collectNudge` performs `IERC20(token).safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amount); s.buffer += amount;` (:149-150) with no balance-delta measurement. The streamer holds a SINGLE POOLED balance per token across every `(batchMinter, token)` pair, while `_settle` caps payouts against the per-stream accounting buffer (`_accrued`, :193-200), not against real custody. The contract NatSpec at :194-196 asserts 'The buffer cap guarantees the streamer can never transfer more than it holds, even if elapsed is large' — that guarantee is PER-STREAM whereas custody is POOLED PER-TOKEN, so it does not hold across pairs. The deploy-script probe at DeployMocks.s.sol:1661 is the only defence anywhere and it is VACUOUS: it runs solely against MockKendu and MockPhUSD, both defined with no transfer fee, so it cannot fail locally. There is no on-chain guard.
impact: For any reward token that is fee-on-transfer, taxed, or reflection-based: (1) the credited buffer immediately exceeds custody; (2) whichever `(batchMinter, token)` pair settles first is paid its full over-stated buffer out of the shared balance, consuming the backing of the other pairs; (3) the later pair's `pullPendingStream` REVERTS on insufficient balance; and (4) because `BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.batchMint` loops `pullPendingStream` over `getNudgeTokens()` inside one transaction (:539), a single tainted token bricks batchMint for ALL reward tokens — the entire mint path, not just the tainted reward. Kendu Inu is a memecoin whose real transfer semantics are unverified, and MockKendu's own NatSpec states the mock is deliberately fee-free because the streamer assumes exact delivery.
attackPath: 1. Owner whitelists a fee-on-transfer / taxed / reflection token as a nudge token via setNudgeTokenWhitelist (non-obvious footgun; Kendu Inu's real transfer semantics are unverified on-chain).

2. A donor calls collectNudge(batchMinter, token, amount); NudgeStreamer.sol:149-150 does safeTransferFrom then `s.buffer += amount` with no balance-delta measurement, so the credited buffer exceeds actual custody by the tax.
3. A second (batchMinter, token) pair is registered on the SAME token. Custody is pooled per token; the cap in _accrued is per STREAM, so total credited buffers now exceed the single pooled balance.
4. Whichever pair settles first is paid its full over-stated buffer out of the shared balance, consuming the other pair's backing.
5. The later pair's pullPendingStream reverts on insufficient balance.
6. batchMint, which loops pullPendingStream over all whitelisted tokens in one tx, now reverts for ALL reward tokens - the whole mint path is down, not just the tainted reward.
evidence: PoC workspace/phoenix-phase-2-staging/test/AuditDevNudgeStreamerFoT.t.sol — 4/4 PASS against the REAL NudgeStreamer with a 5% fee-on-transfer ERC20. (A) buffer 100,000e18 vs custody 95,000e18. (B) two pairs of the same token: buffers 200,000e18 vs pooled custody 190,000e18; pair A settles and the streamer pays out its full 100,000, leaving 90,000 against pair B's 100,000 claim; B's pullPendingStream reverts. (C) a clean token settles fine in isolation while the tainted token reverts — and batchMint shares one transaction. (D) at feeBps==0 the divergence vanishes entirely, confirming the DeployMocks probe passes vacuously by construction. Also confirmed on the live local chain: streamer balance EXACTLY equals the credited buffer for all three tokens, i.e. the condition under which this finding is invisible.
recommendation: Measure the receipt in `collectNudge`: `uint256 before = IERC20(token).balanceOf(address(this)); safeTransferFrom(...); uint256 received = IERC20(token).balanceOf(address(this)) - before; s.buffer += received;` and recompute the rate from `received`. If fee-on-transfer tokens are intended to be permanently out of scope, add an on-chain probe in `registerStream` (which is already owner-gated and is the natural admission point) rather than relying on a deploy-script assert against a mock that cannot fail. Independently, verify the real Kendu token's transfer semantics on-chain BEFORE `setNudgeTokenWhitelist` on mainnet.

classification.c4Criterion: C4 Medium - 'the function of the protocol or its availability could be impacted ... with stated assumptions, but external requirements'.
classification.assetImpact: No theft and no economic loss. Two distinct effects, deliberately rated on the availability axis only: (a) CROSS-PAIR CONSUMPTION - pair A's settlement is paid out of the pooled per-token balance that also backs pair B, so B's backing is consumed. Because Phoenix nudge pots are funded by yield on protocol-owned capital, this is MISALLOCATION between two legitimate recipient pots, NOT a value leak, and is expressly not scored as economic loss (repo rule: externally-derived yield is opportunity cost, not loss). (b) AVAILABILITY BRICK - the under-backed pair's pullPendingStream reverts, and because BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.batchMint loops pullPendingStream over the entire getNudgeTokens() whitelist inside one transaction (verified at top-level HEAD, BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.sol:527-532), a single tainted token bricks the ENTIRE mint path for every reward token. This is the load-bearing impact and it is a protocol-function failure.

classification.likelihood: medium-low as a trigger, high as a consequence once triggered. There is NO external attacker and no unauthorised actor anywhere in the path; the trigger is an owner whitelisting decision. It is nonetheless a genuine Law-3 footgun rather than trusted-owner noise: a competent, non-malicious owner would be surprised that whitelisting one memecoin bricks minting for every reward token, and the contract's own NatSpec at :193-195 tells them the opposite.
classification.assumptions: (1) A fee-on-transfer / taxed / reflection token is whitelisted as a nudge token. (2) For the cross-pair drain specifically, at least two (batchMinter, token) pairs share one token; the single-pair case yields under-delivery and a stuck residual rather than a revert. (3) FoT is IN SCOPE for this family - the C4 'weird ERC-20 / fee-on-transfer' known-invalid predicate does NOT fire, because phoenix-nft-staking story-022 s4.4 documents FoT explicitly and the defect is a first-party accounting bug in NudgeStreamer.sol, not a request for weird-token support.
classification.externalRequirements: Owner must admit a taxed token through setNudgeTokenWhitelist. No timing, MEV, price or third-party dependency.

severityRationale: MEDIUM, matching the auditor's proposal. Held AT medium from both directions. NOT ESCALATED TO HIGH: nothing is stolen and nothing leaves the protocol perimeter - there is no attacker, no external beneficiary, and the shortfall manifests as a REVERT plus a stranded residual, not as extraction. The cross-pair effect moves value between two legitimate protocol-owned pots, which under this repo's standing rule on externally-derived yield is misallocation and never a value leak. The condition is also owner-reversible (de-whitelist the tainted token, or top the streamer up by the accumulated tax) so the brick is not terminal. NOT DEFLATED TO LOW: the availability failure is PROVEN, not argued - PoC workspace/phoenix-phase-2-staging/test/AuditDevNudgeStreamerFoT.t.sol is 4/4 PASS against the REAL NudgeStreamer (case A over-credit, case B cross-pair drain + revert, case C one tainted token reverts the whole loop, case D the divergence vanishes at feeBps==0). Case D is what makes this reportable rather than theoretical: it proves the only defence in the system - the DeployMocks.s.sol:1661 probe - is VACUOUS BY CONSTRUCTION, since it runs solely against MockKendu and MockPhUSD which are both fee-free, so it cannot fail. There is no on-chain guard anywhere. SEVERITY-RAISING FACTOR: the contract NatSpec at NudgeStreamer.sol:193-195 affirmatively asserts 'The buffer cap guarantees the streamer can never transfer more than it holds' - the guarantee is per-STREAM while custody is POOLED PER-TOKEN, so it is false across pairs. Per this repo's standing principle, falsely-exhaustive documentation raises severity rather than lowering it: it is the reason an operator would never think to check, and it is why this does not settle at Low as a documented design constraint. PROPAGATES-TO-MAINNET and verified against top-level submodule HEAD (lib/phoenix-nft-staking/src/NudgeStreamer.sol is byte-identical to the nested pin lib/nft-staking, so this is not a stale-pin artefact).

parkedItemsCarriedForward.title: ERC4626YieldStrategy.previewRedeem / previewDeposit view passthroughs still STATICCALL the underlying vault — the story-060 / YS-01 Tokemak fix is one-directional
parkedItemsCarriedForward.sourceVerification: Read against the TOP-LEVEL submodule HEAD lib/reflax-yield-vault (not a nested stale pin). :73-75 `return vault.previewDeposit(assets);` and :83-85 `return vault.previewRedeem(shares);`, both declared `external view` => Solidity emits STATICCALL. Twenty lines below, :110-115 credits principal via `vault.convertToAssets(sharesReceived)` with an in-source comment naming the exact hazard: 'Use convertToAssets (NOT previewRedeem): convertToAssets is ERC4626-mandated STATICCALL-safe, whereas some real vaults (e.g. Tokemak Autopools) mutate state inside previewRedeem and revert with StateChangeDuringStaticCall when called as an external view.' The authors therefore knew the hazard and hardened ONE call site.
parkedItemsCarriedForward.whyItMatters: Against a real Tokemak Autopool these two views revert for every caller, always; against MockAutoDOLA (plain un-overridden OZ ERC4626) they return a clean number, always. The local rig therefore reports green on the exact behaviour that already bricked this project's YS-swap suite. Blast radius today is UI/keeper reads (no first-party on-chain caller found), which is why this is parked for triage rather than asserted as a Medium.

secondaryGapsInTheSameMockSection: No maxRedeem/maxWithdraw check before `vault.redeem` in _disposeShares (:128-135): against a real Autopool with a liquid reserve below the request, user withdrawals brick. Locally impossible to reproduce.

MockAutoDOLA._updateYield() mints assets into the vault BEFORE super._deposit mints shares, so convertToAssets(sharesReceived) > amount and creditedPrincipal at :115 can EXCEED the deposited amount — the precise opposite of that line's stated intent. Any local invariant asserting 'principal is never over-credited' passes VACUOUSLY. Flagged because a vacuous-harness result is a known repeat failure mode in this repo.
